key_insight: EVENET is a foundation model for particle collision analysis that learns from simulated collisions and transfers across multiple analysis tasks. It also works on real collider data, connecting simulation-based training with experimental use.
problem_solved: Particle collision analysis needs models that can support diverse tasks and remain useful when moving from simulated training data to real experimental measurements.
method: Pretrain EVENET on simulated particle collision data.
Combine self-supervised learning with training guided by physics labels.
Transfer the pretrained model to multiple analysis tasks and apply it to real collider data.
impact: EVENET demonstrates how foundation-model pretraining can support reusable AI for scientific analysis. For AI/ML practitioners, it highlights a combination of self-supervision and domain-specific labels that transfers across tasks and from simulation to real data.
visual_elements: Training pipeline: simulated collisions → self-supervision + physics labels → EVENET.

paper_title: Foundation model for particle collision data analysis
paper_authors: Ting-Hsiang Hsu, Baihong Zhou, Qibin Liu, Yue Xu, Shu Li
